Collect as little as possible

Privacy & Ethics

HIV information can be deeply personal. This public website is designed as an educational resource, not a place to submit medical histories or seek a diagnosis.

Policy ownerRuang Tanpa Stigma

Last updated20 September 2026

ScopePublic website and content library

On this page

  1. 01What is collected
  2. 02Sensitive health data
  3. 03Service boundaries
  4. 04External services
  5. 05Reach measurement
  6. 06Evaluation ethics

01 · Current situation

The public website does not ask readers to create accounts or profiles.

At the time this policy was written, Ruang Tanpa Stigma's public website has no contact form, comments, newsletter, reader accounts, reader login, project-installed third-party analytics or marketing trackers.

The website is served through GitHub Pages. Hosting providers and internet infrastructure may process standard technical data, such as IP addresses or request logs, under their own policies. Ruang Tanpa Stigma does not promise that no technical data is processed outside the project’s control.

02 · Sensitive health data

We do not need someone’s HIV status to provide education.

The public website does not ask for or provide a place to submit:

  • HIV status or diagnosis;
  • viral load or CD4 results;
  • medication information;
  • sexual history;
  • health records;
  • identifying medical information.

Do not place patient data, stories that could identify someone else, or personal health information in editorial drafts. The website repository is public.

03 · Service boundaries

Education, not diagnosis or care.

Ruang Tanpa Stigma is not a clinical service, diagnostic provider, crisis counselling service or emergency service. Website information does not replace individual risk assessment, consultation, diagnosis, treatment or care from a qualified health professional.

Local service details that can change—such as locations, hours, costs, eligibility or availability of PrEP, PEP, ART and testing—will not be published as a directory until they can be verified and dated.

04 · External services

External links have their own policies.

Links to Indonesia’s Ministry of Health, WHO, UNAIDS, LinkedIn, GitHub and other services take readers to third-party websites. Their privacy and accessibility policies apply after a link is opened.

The Instagram link takes readers to Instagram/Meta. Selecting the email link opens the reader’s email application or provider. Information sent voluntarily by email is processed through the sender’s and recipient’s email providers; it is not represented as medically confidential or encrypted communication.

The project email is for general initiative communication, content-correction reports, and appropriate educational collaboration enquiries. Please do not send HIV status, laboratory results, sexual history, medication details, or other sensitive health information by email or Instagram.

If an article includes a YouTube video, the player uses the privacy-enhanced youtube-nocookie.com domain. Opening a video page can still cause the browser to communicate with YouTube. This mode reduces certain cookie use but does not guarantee that no data is exchanged.

05 · Measuring reach

No analytics has been installed.

The Monitoring & Evaluation framework will eventually need reach data, but V2 does not automatically install third-party tracking. At the beginning, aggregate data available from public platforms and manual records may be sufficient.

Before website analytics is considered, the project will compare data needs, cookie behaviour, processing location, retention, anonymization options, respect for Do Not Track, and clarity of disclosure. Any installation requires a separate decision and an update to this policy.

06 · Evaluation ethics

Programme monitoring is not the same as human-subject research.

Measuring outputs, reach, content quality and usefulness for programme improvement is Monitoring & Evaluation. Research involving human participants that aims to produce generalizable knowledge, scientific publication or formal research requires ethical consideration appropriate to its design and context.

Basic usability testing does not need to ask participants for their HIV status. If sensitive feedback is ever collected, purpose, consent, data minimization, secure storage and participant rights must be established first.
